messages:
Sam: Quick sync — I sketched a small set of "safety norms" for the hosting handshake between hosted / dedicated / private. Goal: predictable failures + clear rollback points, not to gate every edge.
Maria: +1. Can you post the minimal invariants?
Sam: Sure. Minimal invariants I care about: 1) tenant identity verified before routing, 2) model variant compatibility checked (quantization / kv layout), 3) cache namespace versioned across deploys, 4) max handshake latency budget and a deterministic fallback.
Josh: For (3) — do we mean TTL-only caches or explicit invalidation on model/manifest change?
Sam: Prefer explicit invalidation when manifest hash changes; TTL as a backstop. Otherwise evictions are unpredictable across hosting modes.
Li: Concrete config suggestion (proto-ish):
```yaml
handshake:
  max_wait_ms: 150
  tenant_verify: strict
  manifest_hash_check: true
  cache:
    version_header: X-Model-Manifest
    invalidate_on_manifest_change: true
    fallback_ttl_ms: 300000
```
Maria: How do we enforce that without coupling control planes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private? We can't call the hosted control plane from private installs.
Sam: Two pieces: 1) the handshake only needs the manifest hash that the control plane publishes into the runtime's local manifest store (signed). 2) For private, customer-managed control plane pushes the same artifact + signature to local store via the same API surface. So runtime verifies signature and hash locally. No cross-calls.
Josh: What about rolling upgrades where manifest changes but old cache entries still in GPUs? We need a soft-evict signal to the runtime.
Li: Runtime should treat manifest_hash change as a hard namespace bump for KV cache keys. Old keys are logically dead; we can lazily free memory. That avoids global synchronous eviction.
Maria: Sounds good. Concern: latency-sensitive paths — handshake max_wait_ms 150 might be too tight for some on-prem networks. Maybe make it configurable per deployment mode with safe defaults.
Sam: Agreed. Default per-mode: hosted=150ms, dedicated=250ms, private=500ms. OpsBot: Note created: CONSTRAINTS-547.
Josh: Also add a graceful rollback trigger: if handshake fails for >N requests in S seconds, route to lower-capacity compatible model variant automatically (and emit an alert).
Sam: Proposal: 5 failures in 60s -> degrade to compatible-variant if available; if not, circuit-break with 503 and clear diagnostic message.
Li: We'll need a small test harness to simulate manifest churn and handshake flakiness across modes. I can add unit tests + a synthetic e2e in staging.
Maria: OK. Next actions: Sam to write RFC with the norm list + config knobs; Li to draft tests; Josh to prototype the cache namespace bump. I'll own rollout plan with canary gating and observability hooks.
Sam: I'll start the RFC tonight. Thx all. :thumbsup:
